# Spec → Test Plan (RPI Plan Gate)

You are producing a **test plan**, not test code. No `pytest`, no `jest`, no scaffolding. This is the **RPI Plan gate** inside the testing phase: the tech lead reviews and approves this plan before any test code is generated by a downstream agent or prompt.

## Input

User story or work item:

> **${input:story:Azure Boards URL/ID, GitHub Issue URL, or pasted user story text}**

Resolve the input as follows:

- **Azure Boards** (`dev.azure.com/...` URL, `AB#1234`, or bare work-item ID) — fetch the work item, including title, description, and acceptance criteria.
- **GitHub Issue** (`github.com/.../issues/123` URL or `#123` in a repo context) — fetch the issue title, body, and any linked acceptance criteria.
- **Pasted text** — use it directly as the spec.

If the spec is ambiguous, missing acceptance criteria, or under-specified, **stop and ask** before drafting cases. Do not invent acceptance criteria.

## Required Output

Produce exactly the sections below, in this order, in Markdown. Use the exact case counts — no more, no less.

### 1. Story Summary
- **Source:** Azure Boards #ID / GitHub Issue #ID / pasted
- **Title:** <one line>
- **User value (one sentence):** As a <role>, I want <capability>, so that <outcome>.
- **Acceptance criteria (verbatim, bulleted):** copy from source; do not paraphrase.

### 2. Scope & Assumptions
- **In scope for this plan:** the behaviors covered by the cases below.
- **Out of scope:** behaviors deferred to other stories or non-functional layers (perf, load, accessibility) unless the spec explicitly demands them.
- **Assumptions:** every assumption you made to interpret the spec. The reviewer must be able to challenge each one.

### 3. Test Plan

Use the table below. Exactly **7 cases**: 1 happy path + 3 edge cases + 2 failure modes + 1 security-relevant case.

| # | Type | Title | Given | When | Then | Linked AC |
|---|------|-------|-------|------|------|-----------|
| 1 | Happy path | ... | ... | ... | ... | AC-x |
| 2 | Edge case | ... | ... | ... | ... | AC-x |
| 3 | Edge case | ... | ... | ... | ... | AC-x |
| 4 | Edge case | ... | ... | ... | ... | AC-x |
| 5 | Failure mode | ... | ... | ... | ... | AC-x |
| 6 | Failure mode | ... | ... | ... | ... | AC-x |
| 7 | Security | ... | ... | ... | ... | AC-x or "cross-cutting" |

**Rules for each row:**
- **Happy path (1):** the primary acceptance criterion executed end-to-end with valid input.
- **Edge cases (3):** boundary values, empty/zero/max inputs, off-by-one, ordering, concurrency, locale/timezone, or other "unusual but legal" inputs. Each must be *distinct* — no near-duplicates.
- **Failure modes (2):** the system must fail safely. Cover at least two of: invalid input, downstream dependency unavailable, timeout, partial write/transaction rollback, permission denied. State the expected error contract (status code, error shape, log/trace expectation).
- **Security-relevant (1):** pick one of: authn/authz bypass attempt, injection (SQL/command/prompt), IDOR/tenant-isolation, secret exposure in logs/responses, replay, or input that triggers excessive resource use. State the expected mitigation in *Then*.
- **Linked AC:** map every case back to an acceptance criterion ID, or mark "cross-cutting" only for the security case when no single AC covers it.

### 4. Coverage Check
- Briefly confirm every acceptance criterion is covered by at least one case. If any AC is uncovered, **flag it** and ask the reviewer whether to add a case or defer the AC.

### 5. Open Questions for the Tech Lead
- Numbered list. Each item is a single, answerable question. If there are none, write "None."

### 6. Plan Gate Status

End with this block verbatim, filled in:

```
RPI Plan Gate
-------------
Plan author: <agent name or model>
Reviewer:    <tech lead — to be filled>
Status:      AWAITING REVIEW
Decision:    [ ] Approved   [ ] Changes requested   [ ] Rejected
Notes:
```

## Hard Rules

- **DO NOT generate test code.** No code blocks containing `def test_`, `it(`, `describe(`, `@Test`, etc. Pseudocode in *Given/When/Then* is fine.
- **DO NOT exceed the case counts.** If you find yourself needing more, pick the strongest representatives and list the rest under *Open Questions*.
- **DO NOT invent acceptance criteria.** If the spec is silent, ask.
- **DO NOT proceed past this gate.** Output ends at section 6. A separate prompt/agent will turn the approved plan into tests.
